title: 7. Amphibious ship to shore (Studland Bay, Dorset; notional)
about: Blue lands a craft from a ship in Poole Bay on to Studland beach. The ship controls a VHF landing-craft net that the craft and a beach party use. Red holds the shore: an ES/DF site on Ballard Down, a second DF across the bay at Hengistbury, a coastal X-band radar at Durlston and a VHF jammer at Swanage, partly masked from the beach by Ballard Down. Grey: harbour VTS and the chain ferry. All values notional.

corridor.note: Worked corridor (amphibious): the landing craft runs in from the ship to Studland beach. Ten-minute layers: the planner weighs the coastal radar (sea clutter with the forecast), red ES and DF, and the Swanage jammer against the craft's net, holds offshore if the surf is over the limit and reports whether the beach party hears the ship direct or needs the craft as a relay. Choose the forecast atmosphere and run first for surf, sea state and the evaporation duct.
